transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I don’t enjoy my job or any of the things I used to love doing anymore, and it’s been like this for weeks now. It just feels like all the joy has been sucked out of my life, and I can't seem to shake it.

Have you had other times in your life when you felt this same loss of interest and low mood for at least two weeks, separated by periods when you felt back to normal? Or did this start after a specific stressful event or major life change?

Looking back, these swings between feeling really revved-up and crashing into these heavy, low periods have actually been happening off and on for several years. This current low spell has been dragging on for about six months now, starting right after a major product relaunch at work wrapped up and my workload went back to normal.

During this low period, have you had any experiences like hearing or seeing things others don’t, or strongly believing things that others say aren’t true? If yes, did those happen only when you were very depressed?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've never seen or heard things that weren't really there, nor have I held onto beliefs that others found untrue.
During this depressive period, have you still been able to keep up with daily responsibilities like work, self-care, and basic tasks, or has the depression made that nearly impossible?

It's been extremely difficult to keep up, and my performance at work has slipped to the point where my manager recently asked if I was okay because I've been missing deadlines. At home, I've been bailing on chores and social plans so much that my husband has had to pick up most of the slack. Even simple, everyday tasks feel completely overwhelming now and take me ages to get through.

When you felt “really revved-up,” did you ever go for several days needing much less sleep and feeling unusually energetic or confident, talking faster, having racing thoughts, or doing impulsive things that caused problems? If so, did those periods last at least 4 days or as long as a week?

Yes, absolutely. During those times I felt incredibly energetic and overconfident, staying up late sketching ideas at midnight and bouncing from one thought to another because I felt like I was the only one who truly understood our brand. These revved-up phases lasted much longer than four days or a week—they would go on for weeks at a time, and they've been happening off and on for several years now.

This pattern supports bipolar affective disorder, current episode mild or moderate depression. Psychotic symptoms were denied.
